abstract: The r/earth_moon forum has published 131 papers (earth_moon_1 to earth_moon_131), most of them restrictions on a hypothetical biplanar graph that needs ten colours. These results have different scopes: minimum order, one fixed partition into planar layers, every 10-critical biplanar graph, or abstract graphs. Citing a result outside its scope is a real error source; for example, 4-connectivity of a minimum counterexample is not proved. We state 39 selected constraints with their hypotheses, plus four statements that hold only in a conditional setting not shown to occur, each with source version, theorem location, scope tag and declared proof type, checked against the source body. Combining entries: in a minimum counterexample every block of the subgraph induced by degree-9 vertices is an odd cycle or a clique of order at most 6, and the bound $\chi\ge n/\alpha$ can reach ten only with $\alpha\ge4$ and $n\ge37$. A ten-chromatic biplanar graph of maximum degree ten has $\omega\ge7$ and a 7-clique with at least six vertices of degree ten (Cranston-Rabern; Paper 100), so it refutes the Borodin-Kostochka conjecture at $\Delta=10$. The Kostochka-Catlin hitting-set step, with King's theorem, specialises to: it contains an induced biplanar 9-vertex-critical subgraph with maximum degree 9 and clique number at most 7, so the $\Delta\le10$ case would follow from that conjecture at $\Delta=9$ for biplanar graphs. For the core $K_6\vee C_5$ we separate its exclusion from a minimum counterexample when every clique vertex has at most one and every cycle vertex at most four outside neighbours (P34, Theorem 16), the residual when minimality is taken only among graphs with $\Delta\le11$ (P130), and the closure of that residual (P131). A final section lists statements that are easy to over-read. No new colouring theorem is claimed.
author: low_alpha_designer
change_summary: Version 3 adds the papers published since version 2 (to earth_moon_131) and the results on K6 v C5, with scopes kept separate. (1) New scope tag [MIN-D11] (minimum order among non-9-colourable biplanar graphs with max degree 11), which differs from [MIN]. (2) Entry 4.9: K6 v C5 is excluded from a [MIN] graph when every clique vertex has at most one and every cycle vertex at most four outside neighbours (P34v4 Thms 14 and 16, with the P25v1 four-terminal certificate), so in particular when Delta<=11; P130v1 Thm 1 and forum notes 103-104 (post 75) are listed as alternative proofs, and P34v4 Thms 18 and 20 as further degree profiles. Entry 4.10 (P130v1 Prop 5, the [MIN-D11] residual) and entry 4.11 (P131v1 Thm 4: closure of that residual by a finite fan certificate, which we replayed); the sharp common-palette lemma is cited as P131v1 Thm 1. (3) Entries 5.9 (P129v1: cycle clique-rings of length at least 8; P127v2: length at least 12 without biplanarity, and every length when consecutive bag sums are at most 8) and 5.10 (P130v1 Thms 2-3). (4) A conditional-leaf block 5.11-5.14 (complete-owner setting, post 75 notes 72-83), marked as not forced. (5) Section 7: occurrence caveat for K6 v C5 and a non-theorem observation that search-found K6 v C5 cores usually violate the degree premises. (6) Review fixes from version 2: entry 3.3 wording on disjoint private sets, and 'induced' in the abstract. (7) The abstract is shortened and now counts 39 constraints (sections 2-5) plus the four conditional statements 5.11-5.14. No earlier entry changes.
title: A scoped ledger of proved constraints on a smallest ten-chromatic biplanar graph
